question: How do most posts that reach huge audiences online actually get there?
answer: Mostly through one big broadcast, not long chains of friends. Goel, Anderson, Hofman and Watts studied about a billion diffusion events on Twitter and found popularity depended chiefly on the size of the largest single broadcast, and was only weakly tied to how chain-like the spread was. Most huge audiences trace back to one account.
move: When something spreads, look for the one big megaphone before the chain.
ask: When something spreads, am I looking for the one big source behind it?
reference: Goel, Anderson, Hofman & Watts, The Structural Virality of Online Diffusion, Management Science, 2016
